locator: cap.3 [69874]: Omne autem quod recipit aliquid ab alio est in potentia respectu illius, et hoc quod receptum est in eo est actus eius
interpretation: Whatever receives something from another is in potency with respect to it, and what is received in it is its act. Read as: when a thing's esse is received in a principle, that principle is not the esse itself, so no esse is received in itself. The sentence correlates receiver as potency with received as act; that this correlation requires two distinct principles is the reading's added step, open and not stated in the sentence. The source then applies the correlation to intelligences whose essence/esse distinction it has already argued, so the passage does not independently defend the step against a proposed self-receiving esse (ATTEMPT-SUBSISTENT-INFINITY-RECEPTION-AUDIT-20261031). 'From another' (causal origin) is not formalized: only reception in a principle is.
